piece_type: Exhibit booth display and brochure at APA 2026 Annual Meeting (investigational drug)

cases.cat: Preapproval promotion of investigational drug (safety/efficacy claims)
cases.heading: (none; body text)
cases.claim: “ALA-3000 Breaks Key Barriers in Ketamine Therapy for TRD” (brochure) | “Sustained-release profile for weeks without pronounced initial burst or dose dumping effect” (brochure) | “Potentially eliminates the mandatory ≥2-hour post-dose on-site monitoring required with ketamine therapies.” (brochure)
cases.context: Investigational drug apparently studied only in Phase 1; booth placed near approved-product booths.
cases.rationale: Conclusory statements represent an investigational new drug as safe and effective for the use under investigation, violating 21 CFR 312.7(a).
cases.check: For an unapproved/investigational product, does the piece make conclusory safety or effectiveness claims or otherwise promote the drug?

cases.cat: Misleading claims about safety (investigational drug; implied superiority)
cases.heading: (none; body text)
cases.claim: “No overall sedative, dissociative, psychosis-like side effects” (exhibit booth display) | “No sedation, dissociation, psychosis-like effects, or commonly ketamine-reported AEs (e.g., blood pressure elevation, urinary toxicity)” (brochure) | “No abuse signals” (brochure)
cases.context: Ketamine is CIII with known risks of sedation, dissociation, respiratory depression, hemodynamic instability, abuse and misuse.
cases.rationale: Represents the investigational drug as safe and superior to approved ketamine therapies without adequate data.
cases.check: Rule: flag absolute safety claims of the form 'No [adverse effect/abuse/side effects]' and 'no ... signals', especially for unapproved products.

cases.heading: (none; body text)
cases.claim: The exhibit booth display did not include any information to indicate that ALA-3000 is an investigational new drug that has not been approved for commercial distribution in the United States.
cases.context: Booth appeared in APA exhibit hall near booths for approved products.
cases.rationale: Absence of investigational status contributes to promotional representation of an unapproved drug.
cases.check: Rule: for investigational products, require an explicit 'investigational / not approved by FDA' statement on every piece.
